title: Revenue Recognition
description: Apply the revenue recognition model to contracts, performance obligations, and transaction prices.
html:
Revenue Recognition

Revenue from contracts with customers is generally recognized using the five-step model in ASC Topic 606.

Core Principle:

Recognize revenue to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration the entity expects to receive.

The Five-Step Revenue Model

Step 1 Identify the Contract
Step 2 Identify Performance Obligations
Step 3 Determine the Transaction Price
Step 4 Allocate the Transaction Price
Step 5 Recognize Revenue

1. Identify the Contract

A contract creates enforceable rights and obligations between the entity and the customer.

Among other criteria, the parties must approve the arrangement, their rights and payment terms must be identifiable, the arrangement must have commercial substance, and collection must be probable.

2. Identify Performance Obligations

A performance obligation is generally a promise to transfer a distinct good or service to the customer.

A promised good or service is distinct when the customer can benefit from it on its own or with other readily available resources and the promise is separately identifiable within the contract.

Example

A company sells equipment together with a separately identifiable one-year maintenance service.

If both are distinct, the equipment and the maintenance service are separate performance obligations.

3. Determine the Transaction Price

The transaction price is the amount of consideration the entity expects to be entitled to in exchange for transferring the promised goods or services.

Consideration may include:

  • Fixed amounts
  • Variable consideration
  • Noncash consideration
  • Other adjustments required by the guidance

Variable Consideration

Variable consideration may result from bonuses, discounts, rebates, refunds, penalties, or similar items.

Variable consideration is included in the transaction price only to the extent that it is probable that a significant reversal of cumulative revenue will not occur when the uncertainty is later resolved.

4. Allocate the Transaction Price

If a contract contains multiple performance obligations, the transaction price is generally allocated based on relative standalone selling prices.

Example

A company sells Product A and Service B together for $900.

Their standalone selling prices are:

Product A = $800 Service B = $200 Total Standalone Selling Prices = $1,000

Product A receives 80% of the transaction price:

$900 × 80% = $720

Service B receives 20%:

$900 × 20% = $180

5. Recognize Revenue

Revenue is recognized when or as a performance obligation is satisfied through transfer of control of the promised good or service to the customer.

Point in Time vs. Over Time

Some performance obligations are satisfied at a specific point in time, while others are satisfied over time.

Over-Time Recognition:

A performance obligation is satisfied over time if one of the applicable criteria is met.

  • The customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits as the entity performs.
  • The entity's performance creates or enhances an asset that the customer controls as the asset is created or enhanced.
  • The entity's performance creates an asset with no alternative use to the entity, and the entity has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date.
Typical Product Sale Often Point in Time
Qualifying Service Contract May Be Over Time

When revenue is recognized over time, the entity recognizes revenue based on an appropriate measure of progress toward complete satisfaction of the performance obligation.

Contract Liability

If a customer pays before the company has transferred the promised goods or services, the company generally records a contract liability rather than revenue.

Example

A customer pays $12,000 in advance for a 12-month service contract.

At the beginning, the company generally records a contract liability.

If the service is provided evenly over the year, monthly revenue would be:

$12,000 ÷ 12 = $1,000 Per Month

Contract Asset

A contract asset may arise when an entity has transferred goods or services but its right to consideration is still conditional on something other than the passage of time.

CPA Exam Memory Rule

Contract ↓ Performance Obligations ↓ Transaction Price ↓ Allocate ↓ Recognize When / As Control Transfers

Key Takeaways

  • Revenue recognition under Topic 606 follows a five-step model.
  • Distinct promised goods and services may be separate performance obligations.
  • Transaction price may include fixed and variable consideration.
  • Transaction price is generally allocated using relative standalone selling prices.
  • Revenue is recognized when or as control transfers to the customer.
  • Advance customer payments generally create a contract liability until the related performance obligation is satisfied.

quiz.prompt: A company sells a product and a separate service for a combined transaction price of $900. The product has a standalone selling price of $800 and the service has a standalone selling price of $200. How much of the transaction price should generally be allocated to the product?
quiz.explanation: The total standalone selling price is $1,000. The product represents 80% of that total, so $900 × 80% = $720 is allocated to the product.
